source_document.body:
The Port of Oakland and heavy-duty charging provider WattEV have opened a public electric truck charging depot, pairing new infrastructure with a planned purchase of 300 Tesla Semis to expand zero-emission freight service across Northern California and beyond.
Officials at a ceremony Monday described the depot as the first of its kind in Northern California. The first batch of trucks is expected before the end of the year, with the remaining vehicles arriving in 2027.
The project represents a northward expansion of electric trucking infrastructure on the West Coast. According to WattEV, heavy-duty truck charging has so far been concentrated largely in Southern California. The Oakland depot is intended to help establish a zero-emission freight corridor connecting the Bay Area with Sacramento, the Central Valley, Nevada and other destinations.
“We’re seeing real progress in transforming how our industry moves goods to and from the Oakland Seaport,” Port of Oakland Executive Director Kristi McKenney said at a port ceremony. “Together with our industry partners, we’re delivering projects throughout Oakland that support cleaner freight operations, healthier communities, and a more sustainable future.”
Charging capacity targets freight schedules
The public depot will be capable of charging 25 medium- and heavy-duty trucks simultaneously at up to 240 kilowatts each, or seven trucks at 1.2 megawatts each.
Its megawatt-charging design is intended to reduce charging stops to 30 minutes or less, a duration project officials describe as comparable to diesel refueling.
The opening puts charging infrastructure in place ahead of the full fleet’s arrival, to begin this year and into 2027.
WattEV also said that, at current high diesel prices, the new electric trucks would cost about half as much to operate as comparable diesel models. The company did not provide a detailed cost breakdown in the announcement.
The 300-truck fleet could represent roughly $87 million in vehicle purchases, based on a reported $290,000 price for the 500-mile Tesla Semi. WattEV has not disclosed its actual purchase price or the total cost of the Oakland charging depot.
WattEV Chief Executive and co-founder Salim Youssefzadeh said the project brings together the port, the Bay Area Air District, Tesla and the California Air Resources Board to expand electric freight options for Northern California truckers.
“Until now, most truck charging infrastructure has been concentrated in Southern California, and the options for electric trucks limited their capability,” Youssefzadeh said. “We’re thrilled to enable zero-emission freight transport from a key port like Oakland.”
Oakland Mayor Barbara Lee said community input helped shape the project, with an emphasis on ensuring that neighborhoods disproportionately affected by pollution benefit from investment at the port.
“Today is a significant milestone for Oakland, our port, and the future of green transportation in California,” Lee said.
Why it matters: Oakland’s project pairs two essential pieces of port electrification: trucks to move freight and charging infrastructure to keep them operating, across Northern California and adjoining region.

Air cargo is heading into peak season with a familiar mix of good news and bad. Global demand was up 6% year over year in October, according to Xeneta , and spot rates averaged $3.11 per kilogram . FreightWaves puts rates up about 30% year over year . On paper, that looks like a strong market. On the ramp, in the warehouse and at the booking desk, it looks like something else: a system straining to move more freight through capacity that rarely sits where shippers need it.
The question for airlines, forwarders and shippers isn’t whether these pressures will ease. Some will, some won’t. The real question is which of them are structural, and which are the cost of running a modern, data-heavy business on technology built for a slower era.
The good news is that a new generation of cloud-native, AI-driven cargo platforms is turning each of these pressures into something carriers can manage, and in many cases monetize.
Capacity is there. It’s just in the wrong place.
Freighter additions remain limited, and passenger belly capacity follows passenger demand, not cargo demand. IATA data show August volumes from Asia to North America up 15% year over year, while Asia–Europe fell 8%. The pressure is concentrated on routes from Vietnam, Thailand and Taiwan to the U.S., while other corridors fly with room to spare.
Airlines can’t reposition aircraft to chase every surge. But they can get far better at seeing and selling the space they already fly. Many carriers still plan cargo capacity against static assumptions: a standard allotment per aircraft type, adjusted by hand when passenger loads or fuel change. AI changes that math. Machine learning models trained on historical flown cargo, passenger and baggage loads, aircraft configuration, fuel and seasonal patterns can predict available belly space flight by flight, days before departure, and refresh that prediction as bookings and passenger counts move. Carriers can release space earlier and with more confidence, and, in general, AI-tuned overbooking lets them sell closer to true capacity without risking offloads. Space that used to fly empty because nobody trusted the forecast becomes sellable inventory.
That’s new revenue with no new aircraft. In a market this tight, it may be the cheapest capacity an airline can add.
Rates are high. Pricing discipline is low.
Elevated spot rates are partly a symptom of disruption elsewhere. Ocean disruptions are among the forces lifting air rates , and container reliability problems keep pushing shippers into emergency airfreight, usually at the last minute and at premium cost. For carriers, that sounds like a windfall. In practice, many still price spot requests through email, spreadsheets and gut feel, approving or rejecting quotes without a clear view of how the flight is actually booking.
AI-powered dynamic pricing gives revenue teams a better answer. Models that read demand curves, booking pace and market rates can recommend a hurdle rate for each flight from two weeks out to departure, and flag which spot requests to accept, counter or decline. Decisions that once took hours of back-and-forth take minutes, and they stay consistent across stations. Carriers capture yield on the flights that will fill and stay competitive on the ones that won’t. Shippers get quicker quotes and fewer surprises. Everyone spends less time negotiating by inbox.
Compliance is now a per-parcel cost
The regulatory picture keeps getting more complicated. Tighter security protocols, shifting tariffs and new advance data requirements are landing at the same time as the end of de minimis exemptions. The U.S. suspended its $800 threshold for all countries on Aug. 29, 2025 , and the EU’s €150 duty exemption ended on July 1, 2026 . Every low-value parcel that once moved duty-free now needs accurate, piece-level data.
This is where legacy cargo systems struggle most. They were built around master air waybills and consolidated freight, not millions of individual orders each carrying its own customs record. Platforms designed around piece-level tracking capture that data once, at booking, and carry it through acceptance, screening, customs and delivery. AI adds another layer of protection, flagging vague descriptions, likely misclassified goods and unusual shipper patterns before a parcel reaches the screening line. Compliance stops being a manual reconciliation exercise and becomes a byproduct of the shipment record.
Fuel and margin pressure punish inefficiency
High and volatile fuel costs keep squeezing carrier margins, and the casualties are mounting. According to IATA fuel prices have had a CAGR of 127.46% for U.S. commercial airline fuel from February to September 2026.
AI-driven load optimization is a quiet lever here. Algorithms that build Unit Load Devices (ULDs) in three dimensions around actual shipment dimensions and weight, rather than a planner’s last-minute best guess, fit more revenue cargo on each departure and cut the offloads that turn into rebooking costs and unhappy customers. Integrated dashboards that put AI forecasts of capacity, revenue and cost side by side let teams spot unprofitable flights before they depart, not after the month closes.
Hubs are congested. Data shouldn’t be.
Runway congestion, overbooked warehouse space, understaffed ground handling teams and paperwork backlogs all slow cargo at major airports. Technology won’t add runways. It can remove much of the friction around them.
Cloud-based cargo platforms with open APIs let forwarders book and track through a single integration instead of juggling carrier portals. Electronic air waybills and real-time status updates cut the phone calls and re-keying that eat handler time, and AI document capture can read the paperwork that still arrives on paper. AI-driven exception alerts for a missed connection, a screening hold or a capacity change surface problems while there’s still time to fix them. And because modern platforms deploy in weeks rather than the 18 to 24 months typical of legacy replacements, carriers don’t have to wait years to feel the benefit.
Small parcels, big opening
The biggest opportunity may be the one legacy cargo systems were never built to see: small-parcel e-commerce. Shoppers now expect next-day or two-day delivery, and ground networks struggle to deliver it coast to coast. Passenger airlines already fly thousands of domestic departures a day with belly space to spare. Connect that capacity to e-commerce shippers, and every passenger flight becomes a parcel route, with no new aircraft required.
The demand is there. E-commerce is driving Asia–Latin America air volumes, which rose 23% year over year in August, according to IATA .
Capturing it takes parcel-native technology: online booking, piece-level tracking from booking to doorstep, API connections to retailers and last-mile partners, and AI that predicts which flights will have room for parcels tomorrow. Carriers that get there can launch a parcel product in weeks, earn revenue on space that would otherwise fly empty, and compete for a share of a delivery market that ground carriers have long owned.
The opportunity hiding in the squeeze
Every pressure on this list raises the cost of doing air cargo the old way. Customers and prospects reward carriers that can see their capacity clearly, price it intelligently, comply automatically and move freight without friction. In cargo, AI is moving out of the pilot phase and becoming the operating layer that makes all of that possible.
The airlines that come out of this cycle stronger won’t necessarily be the ones with the most freighters. They’ll be the ones that treat every passenger flight as a cargo opportunity, and run it on cloud-native, AI-driven technology built for the market they’re actually in.

SmartKargo is the AI-powered, cloud-based platform that turns airlines into world-class cargo carriers, with cargo management, e-commerce, and AI in one system. Our cargo ERP runs the entire shipment lifecycle, from booking and acceptance to handling, tracking, and last-mile delivery. Our e-commerce solutions let airlines launch parcel products in weeks and connect directly to online retailers. Our AI applications forecast capacity and demand, guide pricing, and optimize load plans, so airlines capture revenue that legacy systems leave on the table. Trusted by airlines across North America, Latin America, India, and beyond, SmartKargo is making every flight a cargo opportunity. Photo: Volkswagen
The largest European automaker of them all is preparing a powertrain update for its flagship hatchback, which can also be had as a family-oriented longroof. Come summer 2027 for model year 2028, the Golf R should gain the e-charger and variable-geometry turbo from the newly redesigned T-Roc R crossover, bringing a different approach to torque delivery while complying with Euro 7 regs.
Reinhold Ivenz, namely the head of the R go-faster division, suggested the upcoming change to British motoring publication Auto Express during the launch of the 2027 model year T-Roc R . According to Ivenz, the Golf R will pack a bigger punch from lower engine speeds, improving acceleration from a standing start.
Considering the well-known oversimplification that puts torque ahead of horsepower, that certainly sounds like more torque earlier in the rev range. Truth be told, horsepower actually governs both acceleration and top speed. Gearing may let you trade engine speed for twisting force at the wheels, but a transmission does not multiply horsepower.
Having made that clear, a twincharged engine has an inherent advantage over using only a turbocharger. Exhaust-driven turbos are usually bad at producing instant boost before exhaust gases build up, creating turbo lag while requiring more revs to deliver maximum torque and power.
The electric supercharger in the T-Roc R, which is more efficient than Volvo's belt-driven Eaton TVS Roots-type blower, uses the 48-volt system to compress intake air before the exhaust-gas turbocharger wakes up.
Filling the boost gap results in 420 Newton-meters (310 pound-feet) from 1,900 revolutions per minute compared to 2,100 for the outgoing Golf R, peak torque that stays relatively flat until the tacho reads 5,250 revolutions per minute. Peak power arrives 150 revs later, at 5,750 instead of 5,600 revolutions per minute, because torque starts tapering off earlier in the rev range.
Photo: Volkswagen Volkswagen calls these mills EA888 evo4 in the Golf R's case, and EA888 evo5 in the T-Roc R. Both make 333 ps (328 hp) at full chatter, and both rely on iron blocks for extra strength. To recap, two compressors perform complementary jobs in the new-gen engine. The electrically-driven unit supports low-speed grunt while the VTG-type turbo supplies the airflow needed as both engine load and exhaust flow increase.
To satisfy Euro 7 regulations, the EA888 evo5 further benefits from a direct fuel injection system that operates at up to 500 bar instead of 350 bar. The 150-bar jump atomizes the dinosaur juice into a finer mist, improving combustion efficiency while increasing knock resistance under high boost.
Volkswagen also uses the Miller cycle, which closes the intake valves early during the intake stroke to cool the trapped air inside the cylinders before compression starts. The expanded and cooled air drops combustion temperatures, which is way more efficient than dumping excess fuel into the cylinders. In the T-Roc R, the combustion system is designed to maintain a lambda 1 air-fuel ratio throughout its operating range.
As if the aforementioned weren't enough, the engine that will power the Golf R twins from mid-2027 also replaces the conventional alternator and starter motor with a starter-generator thingy that runs on 48 volts. Similar to the T-Roc R, the Golf will continue using a seven-speed tranny of the DCT variety in combination with the R Performance rear torque splitter-type 4MOTION all-wheel-drive system.
While the rear axle may get the same 50 percent torque split as regular 4MOTION, the rear torque splitter sends up to 100 percent of that rear-axle torque to either rear wheel for better cornering. Said rear-axle setup also enables Drift and Nurburgring-focused operating modes.
Drift mode forces 100 percent of the rear axle's torque to the outside rear wheel, overdriving it during a turn to kick out the rear end into a slide. Nurburgring mode, by comparison, maximizes corner-exit speeds by carefully balancing torque between the left and right rear wheels.

Man Pulls Off Heist, Buys 2019 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 Coupe 3ZR ZTK for $158,000
19 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
The market for used C7 Corvette ZR1s is fascinating. Manual examples are fetching ridiculous sums of money, sometimes selling for nearly 2x their MSRP. Meanwhile, the automatic versions are considerably more affordable, which of course makes sense to a certain extent. That being said, this Arctic White example with "almost delivery miles" selling for $158,000 at auction was an absolute steal. I'm a little speechless.
Back in May, we saw a pretty much identical model, albeit with the 7-speed manual gearbox, sell for $275,000 - and it had 1,600 miles on the clock. Then, in June, another 2019 ZR1 7-speed went for $242,000 with just under 8,000 miles on its supercharged LT5 V8. I get how collectible this car is with a manual transmission, but to go from that... to $158,000 on a car that's only covered 201 miles is absolutely incredible.
So yes, this thing was stolen like it just left the set of an Ocean's Eleven movie. This thing is more "stolen" than the Declaration of Independence in Nicolas Cage's National Treasure movie. This thing is... okay, alright, I think you got the point.
In terms of specs, you've got everything you need on this car, which is finished in Arctic White with an Adrenaline Red leather and black microsuede interior. Personally, I like the contrast, especially with the exposed carbon fiber elements and Carbon Flash 19" front and 20" rear wheels. It's a gorgeous spec, although surprisingly, I'd probably take Torch Red over Arctic White. At least on the C7 Corvette. On the C8, it would be the other way around.
The ZTK package is responsible for that massive adjustable rear wing, but also the front splitter end caps, stiffer springs, and the revised Magnetic Ride Control tuning. The wing is actually bolted directly to the chassis, which immediately tells you just how serious of a car this is.
Other exterior highlights include the removable carbon fiber roof panel, vented carbon fiber hood, xenon headlights, quad exhaust outlets, plus carbon ceramic brakes with red Brembo calipers.
Moving along to the interior, that's where we'll find the heated and ventilated GT bucket seats, carbon fiber trim, a Bose sound system, sat-nav, dual-zone automatic climate control, a head-up display, the carbon fiber and microsuede steering wheel, and more.
Photo: Bring a Trailer As for performance, the supercharged 6.2-liter LT5 V8 is pushing 755 horsepower and 715 lb-ft of torque to the rear wheels via an eight-speed automatic transmission and an electronic limited-slip differential. According to GM, the C7 ZR1 can hit 60 mph (97 kph) in 2.85 seconds, but in reality, think more like 3 seconds flat. And that's with the automatic transmission. The 7-speed manual variant should be a tiny bit slower, obviously.
Ultimately, this is an incredible purchase for $158k. And I understand the appeal of manual transmissions on supercars as well as the next guy, but there's no way I'd spend $80k+ on the same car just to shift gears myself.

Ineos Grenadier and Quartermaster to Be Made in the USA Starting in 2028
6 photos
Photo: Ineos
On the market for about four years already, the Ineos Grenadier has managed to establish a sort of cult following for itself. Built as a modern-day off-road vehicle with heavy Land Rover influences, the nameplate managed to conquer first and foremost the hearts and minds of American buyers.
It is from there that the bulk of the sales, some 70 percent, come from. It kind of makes sense, then, why Ineos is about to move production to the USA.
Currently assembled in France, at the Hambach plant that a long time ago was responsible for putting together the smart city cars, the Grenadier SUV, but also its Quartermaster double-cab pickup version, will roll off American production lines as soon as 2028.
The British company, whose name is best known in the petrochemicals, specialty chemicals, and oil products industries, announced this week that it has already shortlisted several potential production sites in the U.S., and says it will announce the final location within the next few months.
Ineos never said directly how many Grenadiers and Quartermasters it sells on an yearly basis (the rumor mill puts that at around 10,000 units per year), but, as stated, the bulk of the orders, 70 percent of them, come from North America.
It makes sense, then, for the carmaker to pack up and leave for friendlier shores, looking not only to be closer to its main client pool, but also to tap into more markets as it seeks to expand its business. And so hyped are the Brits about it that they call the move the biggest moment in their history.
As for the Hambach facility it now operates, Ineos says it is discussing letting it go to Chinese auto giant BYD . Should the two parties reach an agreement on that, the SUV and truck will continue to be produced there in the medium term, probably until the U.S.-based facility is ready.
As a reminder of what the Grenadier is, we're dealing with a boxy SUV with an attitude that would never back out of a fight with the more established names of off-roading. Built on a steel ladder chassis employing long-travel suspension on both ends, it rocks a 3.0-liter straight-six engine sourced from BMW rated at 278 horsepower and 332 lb-ft of torque.
On the American market, Ineos lists four versions of the Grenadier at the time of writing. The main model, called, somewhat ironically, Station Wagon, goes for $71,750, while the Quartermaster pickup variant ups that to $86,300.
An intermediate version called Helmsman is listed at $78,995, and there is also a limited-edition version in the works. The Brits call it the Arcane Works Detour, and only 200 of them will be made.
What is Arcane Works, you ask? That would be an Ineos offshoot that will handle special versions of the SUV, but will also work as a testbed for new technologies, systems, and designs for future vehicles.

By Alexander Whiteman
24 November 2026
Shippers risk undermining their supply chain resilience by awarding transport contracts primarily on price, with increasingly little protection offered by logistics operators when costs rise or capacity constraints hinder movements.
Chris Clowes, executive director of Scala, said while companies often sought to diversify transport suppliers to reduce exposure to disruption, that approach could create a false sense of security if providers are operating on commercially unsustainable rates.
He told The Loadstar : “Having two transport providers on a particular lane may look like sensible contingency planning, but if both have won business by bidding at unsustainably low rates in a procurement exercise, how resilient is the arrangement?
“What happens when costs increase, or capacity becomes constrained? Logistics decision-makers should consider the commercial sustainability of suppliers, as well as their operational capability.”
Rather than judging resilience on the number of suppliers they use, Mr Clowes said shippers needed to assess just how genuinely independent and commercially viable their alternative arrangements were.
He argued that procurement decisions should account for the financial sustainability of logistics providers alongside their operational capabilities, noting the issue reflects a wider problem with how companies approach supply chain resilience.
This, he said was evident in the tendency to concentrate on individual risks rather than examining dependencies that could undermine contingency arrangements. And he pointed out that having multiple suppliers mattered little if they were exposed to the same disruption.
“Having two suppliers isn’t necessarily a resilient solution if they are both in the same location and that region experiences a prolonged drought, because while you have diversified your suppliers, you have not addressed the underlying risk,” he explained.
“Resilience means understanding where the real risks and dependencies sit, testing whether contingency arrangements are genuinely independent, and ensuring that alternative arrangements are commercially and operationally viable.”
Despite increased awareness of supply chain risks, Mr Clowes said he was concerned that too many companies continued to respond to disruption as it happened, rather than testing whether their supply chains could withstand different scenarios.
However, he said if they were able to ensure the resilience of their own business model, smaller forwarders had an opportunity to differentiate themselves by offering reliable service, based on flexibile and strong customer relations.
“Smaller operators can often be more agile and responsive than larger organisations – particularly where they have strong local knowledge and established relationships. That flexibility has real commercial value,” he added.

CoolfFly Nails the First-Ever Personal eVTOL Inter-Island Flight in the Maldives
8 photos
Photo: CoolFly
No speedboats, no choppers, no traffic, and no harmful emissions – this is what the future of tourist air mobility could like in popular island destinations like the Maldives, and this personal electric aircraft from China is already ahead of the game.
CoolFly, the Chinese brand behind what promises to be one of the most exciting lineup of personal aircraft, is wasting no time in proving what its products are capable of. Most recently, the Hangzhou-based company has enjoyed a very prosperous debut in the Maldives, complete with flight demonstrations that are making history.
It all happened during three full days of public demonstrations, organized by the Ministry of Development, Transportation, and Commerce in Maldives, together with the Chinese embassy in Maldives. CoolFly has also attended Expo Maldives 2026, a fruitful event that ended in two strategic collaborations for the Chinese brand – one with aviation operator Skyline Aviation, and another with CMBGA, a Chinese-Maldivian commercial association.
The highlight of this Maldives debut was the demonstration flight over open water, carried out impeccably by the Dream ST, CoolFly’s personal eVTOL (electric vertical takeoff and landing). The aircraft flew from Malé to Villimalé, covering just under two miles (3 km) over open water.
This was heralded as the first-ever inter-island flight carried out by a personal eVTOL in the Maldives, demonstrating a new era of air mobility – faster, cleaner, more efficient, and a lot more exciting.
Maldives officials are obviously interested in the potential of aircraft like the CoolFly Dream ST for the future of island mobility, and this first step could lead to very exciting prospects – perhaps not too far in the future, these Chinese personal eVTOLs will become a regular sight in the Maldives islands.
In terms of regulations, the Dream ST (Seated Configuration) falls under the FAA Part 103 Ultra-Light aircraft category. Purpose-built for individual flight, the Dream ST combines foldable design for easy transport with all-electric propulsion and a complex safety system.
The proprietary NA80 flight control system promises a seamless flight experience, backed by s two redundant flight control units, each featuring three aviation-grade “inertial measurement units” (IMUs), for millisecond-level fault detection. The Dream ST is intended for short-distance flights of 20 to 30 minutes, boasting a maximum speed of 43 mph (70 kph), coupled with a maximum capacity of 110 kg (242 lbs).
CoolFly’s unique lineup of personal aircraft also includes the Urban, a unique standing-configuration model also built for individual flight. There’s also the Dream Pro, a beefed-up version of the Dream ST, targeting other sectors beyond personal aviation, including multiple defense applications.
This past summer, CoolFly has officially introduced the Dream ST to the American public at EAA AirVenture Oshkosh, and is currently looking to establish an official distribution network across the US, as well as other continents. source_document.body:
A free online platform built by a veteran truck driver to help truckers find parking, roadside repairs and other services has exploded to more than 12,000 listings nationwide.
Shawn Gresham , founder of Trucking Life With Shawn , said the directory has grown rapidly since its public launch in October, when it listed 2,031 truck parking locations across 45 states and 259 roadside repair and towing providers.
“I feel like this thing’s tied to a rocket,” Gresham told FreightWaves. “It’s crazy how this thing is blowing up so fast.”
The latest expansion follows an integration with Truck Parking Club , which added thousands of parking locations to Gresham’s directory and allows drivers to access paid parking reservations through the platform.
The growth is also generating business for some roadside service providers.
Chris Brown, owner of Brown’s Diesel Repair & Towing in Tunnel Hill, Georgia, said his company has experienced an 15% increase in call volume since joining the directory.
“We’ve gained probably, I’d say, around 15% call volume,” Brown told FreightWaves. “It’s working. It’s showing up.”
Brown said customers have specifically mentioned finding his business through Gresham’s website, something he hasn’t consistently experienced with other directories where he advertises.
Drivers help build roadside repair network
Gresham, a 17-year trucking veteran, said the fastest-growing portion of his platform has been its roadside repair, tire service and heavy-duty towing directory.
In a Nov. 12 update, Gresham reported 2,555 repair and roadside service listings, compared with just 259 when FreightWaves first reported on the platform in October.
The directory also included 1,946 truck stops, 801 heavy towing companies, 259 weigh stations and 164 CAT scales at that time.
Gresham said many of the repair listings originate with drivers who recommend businesses they have used during breakdowns.
He described drivers submitting recommendations for repair shops that responded quickly, provided reliable service or helped them during overnight emergencies.
Rather than automatically publishing those submissions, Gresham said his team checks the business information, reviews public feedback, contacts the provider and verifies the location.
“We verify the GPS pin to make sure it’s in the right location,” Gresham said. “And then we approve it.”
He said the volume of submissions has increased enough that he has hired additional people to help review listings.
The platform is designed around interstate exits, allowing drivers to search by state, highway and travel direction to locate repair providers and parking areas.
Gresham said his goal is to eventually have at least one free repair provider listing available at every interstate exit where services exist.
Shawn Gresham, founder of TruckingLifeWithShawn.com, said the directory has grown to more than 12,000 listings of truck parking locations, as well as roadside repair and towing providers, since it launched in October. (Photo: Courtesy)
Georgia towing operator reports more business
Brown, who has worked in towing for 24 years and operated his own business since 2018, said finding trustworthy roadside assistance remains a challenge for truck drivers, particularly independent owner-operators.
He said drivers sometimes encounter inexperienced providers, unexpected charges or repair services that cannot perform the work they advertise.
Brown believes having parking, towing, repair and fuel information available through one website can simplify decisions during breakdowns.
He recalled a recent incident involving a truck with a damaged wheel bearing. The driver needed to arrange towing, locate a repair facility and find somewhere to leave the trailer.
The driver initially attempted to use several websites to coordinate the arrangements, Brown said.
After Brown recommended Gresham’s directory, the driver was able to locate the necessary services more easily.
“He said, ‘that was so simple,'” Brown said. “I have four different webpages pulled up trying to find somewhere to park the trailer, somebody to work on it.”
Brown said the driver was able to coordinate parking and repair arrangements using the directory, illustrating how consolidating information can help when a truck is disabled.
Brown also said the directory has introduced his company to potential customers who previously might not have found it.
He said other towing operators have contacted him to ask whether participating in the platform has been worthwhile.
“Once I told them that it works, and we’ve picked up call volume, now they’re interested,” Brown said.
Free for drivers, paid placements for businesses
Gresham said drivers can use the directory without creating an account or paying subscription fees.
The website generates revenue through paid featured placements for repair businesses, book sales and affiliate arrangements with Truck Parking Club.
Businesses can receive a free basic listing, while companies seeking greater visibility along a highway corridor can purchase expanded placement.
Gresham said featured corridor placements cost $99 per month without a long-term contract.
Brown’s Diesel Repair & Towing is among the businesses paying for expanded placement along Interstate 75 in Georgia.
Gresham said Brown’s listing covers approximately 60 exits, allowing drivers searching along that stretch of highway to find the business.
He emphasized that paid placement does not exempt providers from complaints or negative feedback.
Gresham said businesses receiving repeated complaints about poor service could lose their featured status.
The platform’s business model is designed to generate revenue from commercial listings and parking referrals while keeping its core driver tools free, he said.
Truck Parking Club integration expands directory
The latest increase in listings follows an agreement to integrate Truck Parking Club’s parking inventory into the platform.
Gresham said the integration expanded the directory to more than 12,000 listings, including parking locations that drivers can reserve through Truck Parking Club.
The integration also allows drivers to identify parking facilities that may be several miles from an interstate exit, rather than only locations immediately adjacent to the highway.
Gresham said he receives affiliate compensation when drivers reserve parking through the arrangement.
The expanded inventory is expected to support a truck navigation system and trip planner that Gresham is developing.
The GPS system remains in testing with 87 drivers, and Gresham said approximately 7,200 people have joined a waiting list.
He is targeting New Year’s Eve for its public release.
The planned navigation system will incorporate parking locations, repair providers and trip-planning features into a single application.
Gresham said the Android version has progressed through the Google Play process, while work continues on an Apple version.
Platform traffic grows
Gresham said activity on the directory has increased significantly since its launch.
He reported that daily clicks have risen from approximately 32 to more than 1,000.
Gresham said around 2,800 people have subscribed to receive diesel price information by email.
The website also provides CDL practice tests, educational materials and hours-of-service calculation tools.
Gresham, who is also establishing Trucking Life Academy in Dalton, Georgia, said the school’s opening remains pending final approval from the Georgia Department of Driver Services.
For Brown, the directory’s appeal is its ability to help drivers and service providers connect without requiring truckers to search numerous websites during a breakdown.
“I would refer to it as a one-stop website,” Brown said.
Gresham said the rapid growth has exceeded his initial expectations, but the goal remains to make useful information readily available to working drivers.
“Drivers are happy. Everybody’s happy,” he said.
Why it matters: Shawn Gresham, founder of TruckingLifeWithShawn.com, said his platform is helping connect truckers with parking and roadside assistance while offering independent repair and towing businesses another way to reach customers without charging drivers subscription fees.

For most manufacturers , the honest answer is no. A survey published in August 2026 found that 53% of manufacturing CEOs say their business could not keep running for three weeks during a major supply chain shock, and 80% believe up to a fifth of revenue would be at risk if their top three suppliers were disrupted for just two weeks. Closing that gap in 2027 does not start with buying more stock. It starts with better supplier management in direct materials procurement : data people can trust, visibility beyond the first tier and responses agreed before trouble arrives.
Why is supplier risk hiding beyond tier one?
What’s Related
Most manufacturers know their direct suppliers well; far fewer know who supplies those same suppliers. McKinsey’s latest supply chain risk survey found that 95% of companies can see risks at tier one, but only 42% can see into tier two or beyond. Unfortunately, that unmonitored area is also where the next disruption is most likely to start.
The practical first step for savvy procurement leaders to risk-proof the organization is not to take on the whole ecosystem, but to focus on the components and parts whose absence would actually stop the line. For each, they should build a short profile: approved suppliers and the sites they ship from, lead times, stock cover, qualified alternatives and a named owner. Then they should ask critical suppliers to disclose their own key sources.

Can AI-powered procurement software close the gap in 2027?
It can, but only on solid foundations. Supplier and part data need a single owner and common identifiers across every plant and ERP system. Then AI -enabled procurement software earns its keep: reconciling duplicate records, mapping sub-tier suppliers, revealing where several critical parts converge on one source or port , and watching for financial distress, sanctions or logistics delays. People remain responsible for acting on what it finds, so it is important to set clear rules on what AI may recommend, what it may execute and who approves.
Michael Roesch
How will regulation reshape supplier collaboration next year?
Traceability is increasingly becoming a cost line. Since April 2026, US Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminum and copper apply to the full value of affected imports , and in August the UFLPA Entity List grew by 43 companies, including aluminum and copper producers. For businesses trading with Europe, the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) calls for traceability down to the individual plot of land for large and medium-sized operators, the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) has applied since 12 August 2026 and the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD) ill still require the largest companies to carry out supply chain due diligence from 2029. Building origin data into supplier onboarding and part records now is far cheaper than retrofitting it when a customer or customs officer asks.
What should manufacturers agree before the warning lights flash?
Most manufacturers monitor supplier risk; fewer have decided what happens when an alert fires. For each trigger, whether a quality failure, a sanctions listing, a cyber incident or a port delay, it is important to agree who responds, what action follows and which alternatives are already qualified.
Cost, risk, resilience and compliance will still define supply chain performance in 2027. What will separate manufacturers is how early they spot trouble and how quickly they act. The route isn’t exciting new kit: tidy the data, map the supply base, connect planning to sourcing and agree the rules for people and machines alike. Those who start now will be best placed when the next shock arrives.
Michael Roesch is General Manager, Manufacturing at JAGGAER

View of the Richmond Hill property in South Dakota. Credit: Dakota Gold.
By: Northern Miner Staff November 24, 2026
Dakota Gold (NYSE-A: DC) expects its Richmond Hill project in South Dakota to produce 12% more gold annually than projected last year, even as lower recoveries and a shorter mine life cut the metal that the company plans to sell by 40%. The stock dropped. Initial capital rose 40% to $538 million (C$773 million) for an open-pit, heap-leach operation that would produce 171,000 oz. of gold annually and run for nine years instead of 17, Dakota said Monday in a prefeasibility study (PFS). Even so, the company raised its base-case after-tax net present value to $2 billion, compared with $1.6 billion in a 2025 assessment. It used a 5% discount rate in both cases.
The new study “further de-risks and re-confirms Richmond Hill as one of the few advanced development projects globally, with commercial production targeted for 2030,” BMO Capital Markets mining analyst Andrew Mikitchook said Tuesday in a note.
Dakota’s “new conservative mine plan significantly reduces technical risks at the mine through better informed drilling and metallurgical testing,” he added.
Shares of Dakota plunged 8% to $4.02 Tuesday morning in New York, valuing the company at about $539 million. They have traded between $3.96 and $7.25 over the past year.
Historic mine
Located about 320 km west of South Dakota’s capital, Pierre, Richmond Hill is part of a 180-sq.-km land package controlled by the company near the historic Homestake mine. It hosts a large oxide gold system amenable to conventional open-pit mining and heap leach processing.
Homestake produced about 40 million oz. of gold during more than 145 years of mining. It ceased operations in 2002.
Dakota Gold co-chair Robert Quartermain previously built Pretium Resources and developed the Brucejack mine in British Columbia before agreeing to be bought by Newcrest – now Newmont Mining (TSX: NGT; NYSE: NEM) – for about C$3.5 billion ($2.5 billion) in 2021. He formed Dakota Gold the following year to explore in South Dakota.
At a new, higher assumed gold price of $3,500 an oz., Dakota projects a 71% internal rate of return. Using $2,750 gold, the new valuation is $1.25 billion against last year’s $2.15 billion. Dakota’s new plan assumes a 72.4% gold recovery, down from 85.1%, and cuts lifetime payable production to 1.56 million oz. from 2.6 million ounces. Reclassifying material previously considered suitable for heap leaching took about 1 million oz. of gold out of the plan, Mikitchook said. He cut his share price target to $10 from $11 while maintaining his outperform rating.
Larger crushers
Proven and probable reserves as of Nov. 23 totaled 119.6 million tonnes at 0.56 gram gold and 6.61 grams silver per tonne for 2.16 million oz. of gold and 25.4 million oz. of silver. Dakota, which used $2,600 gold to calculate reserves, estimates all-in sustaining costs at $1,289 an oz., including South Dakota’s severance tax. Larger crushers and the cost of building the first section of a leach pad in a steep-sided valley account for much of the increase in initial capital, Vice-President of Project Development Mike Eiselein said Monday on an investor call. Dakota is drilling higher-recovery breccia to try to add at least 10% to reserves for a feasibility study due in mid-2027. It aims to start production in 2029, subject to permits and a construction decision.
The feasibility study and permitting “are the next de-risking steps,” Scotiabank mining analyst Eric Winmill said Tuesday in a note.

2028 Honda CR-V's New Mid-Size Platform Features Nearly 40% High-Strength Steel
10 photos
Photo: Honda
Japanese automaker Honda is rolling out a new vehicle platform, starting with the Avancier three-row SUV. To be used by the next CR-V, Accord, and Civic, this C- and D-segment architecture prides itself on controlled structural flex designed to manage tire loads while cornering, thus giving the suspension a better chance of doing its job while keeping curb weight under control.
The modular platform is described by its maker as having five sections connected by three fixed dimensions. With this arrangement, many Honda and Acura models can share large portions of the underlying structure while accommodating different vehicle heights, ground clearances, and driving positions.
An interesting part of its design is the New Handling Stability Rigidity Management system, which deliberately varies body stiffness in accordance with the loads individual areas must handle. While increasing panel thickness and strengthening joints may come as a sensible approach to improving rigidity, adding weight compromises tire behavior when cornering.
The second-largest Japanese automaker by global sales after Toyota argues that excessive stiffness can make it harder to manage how the tires behave when the suspension loads and unloads. Based on this information, engineers developed areas where controlled deformation smoothens load transfers.
Large project leader and Avancier chief engineer Hidenori Hamashima underlined that his team targeted nearly twice the vertical rigidity at the damper mounts compared to the previous-gen platform. They also used CAE to explore ways of controlling vibration through component stiffness instead of adding sound-deadening material everywhere. The rear brake caliper's relocation forms part of that effort.
Photo: Honda How come? As it happens, Honda moved the rear calipers from behind the rear axle toward the front, bringing them closer to the vehicle's center of rotation. This move reduces inertial inputs, limiting road noise without adding weight through sound-deadening measures. The body-in-white structure, on the other hand, is now made of nearly 40 percent high-tensile steel.
Said high-tensile steel is listed with 980 megapascals of tensile strength, a grade that is strong enough to prevent cabin intrusion during severe crashes while being ductile enough to be stamped into complex shapes without cracking. Because 980 MPa steel is stronger than conventional mild steel, thinner sheet gauges achieve similar structural load capacities.
For this platform, Honda established minimum thickness requirements for each structural member according to stiffness and NVH targets. The Japanese manufacturer also redesigned the front suspension, dropping the steel extension previously mounted ahead of the subframe. Aluminum front lower arms and knuckles are featured, reducing weight and road noise.
For the damper mounts, Honda decided on a crimped construction that increases rigidity without adding extra material. The connections between the knuckles and hub bearings have been stiffened, and suspension geometry was revised for improved lateral rigidity at tire contact points.
Photo: Honda
Then there's the electric power steering system, which receives a torsion bar with greater torsional rigidity for improved stability. Out back, the curved trailing arms have been replaced with straighter components. Honda further reshaped the lower arms with flatter undersides, all in the name of aero.
The rear lower arms now boast a double-plate and double-plate arrangement, reducing weight while allowing shorter arms to improve braking stability. As far as the engine compartment is concerned, Honda achieved a staggering 90 percent commonality across all of this platform's applications.
Shared parts include mounting brackets, wiring, and piping, with Honda claiming a 10-kilo (22 pounds) weight saving to boot. Honda standardized the high-voltage battery position beneath the second-row seats across both SUVs and sedans. The current CR-V and Accord hybrids carry them in the spare tire-pan area and under the rear seats, respectively.
Honda paid attention to the driver's relationship with the steering wheel and pedals as well. The company's so-called skeletal standard puts 140 millimeters (5.5 inches) between the footrest and the loud pedal, and the footrest angle moves close to the accelerator pedal's angle. Honda uses two distinct footrest angles to account for the different seating positions of SUVs and sedans.
The steering wheel angle, meanwhile, increases by one degree. Its telescopic adjustment range grows by 10 mils (0.4 inches). Together, both changes enable a more comfortable driving posture by allowing drivers to keep their arms more relaxed.

Descartes Systems Group has launched Descartes Spot , a new tool that helps freight forwarders quickly get spot-rate quotes for customers. The company says forwarders can answer 90% of customer quote requests in 30 seconds or less.
What’s Related
The cloud -based tool is part of Descartes' broker and forwarder enterprise systems suite. It pulls live carrier rates, schedules, fees, surcharges, and transit times into one place, so sales teams don't have to build each quote by hand. Users enter a port pairing and immediately get several shipping options, each with routes, schedules, transit times and fully calculated costs.
That's different from how many forwarders quote today. Pricing a spot shipment often means digging through carrier websites, plugging numbers into spreadsheets, and waiting hours or even days to send an answer back.
RELATED: Women in Supply Chain: Cyndi Brandt of Descartes Systems Group
Why speed matters
“Speed and transparency are real competitive differentiators in freight forwarding,” said Henning Voss, VP of Product Management at Descartes. “Forwarding is a fast-moving, high-pressure business . Sales teams are under significant strain, and facing huge volumes of requests from customers that require manual, time-consuming work. In a competitive market, the first credible offer often wins.”
Voss said the goal is to let forwarders reply while a deal is still on the table. “This means forwarders can respond while the opportunity is still live and put their energy where it counts: their market knowledge, their relationships, and the deal itself.”
How Spot helps freight forwarders
Along with faster quotes, Descartes Spot lets teams:
Give customers multiple routing and departure options across trade lanes
Save, manage, send, and track quotes in one place
Let business development staff build quotes on their own, without waiting on operations
Set pricing controls to protect margins
Check prices against the market using benchmarking from Xeneta
That last point matters for forwarders worried that faster quoting means underpricing. Xeneta's rate data lets a sales rep compare a quote to the market before sending it.
Forwarders as sales shops
Ken Wood, EVP of Product Management at Descartes, said the launch reflects how the forwarding business is changing.
“Leading freight forwarders are increasingly operating as growth-focused sales organizations, where responsiveness and customer experience play a larger role in winning business,” Wood said. “By removing the delays associated with manual spot quoting, Descartes Spot helps forwarders respond to more opportunities, improve win rates and drive profitable growth.”

Posted By: Colin McClelland November 24, 2026
Seabridge Gold’s (TSX: SEA; NYSE: SA) bid to build one of Canada’s largest undeveloped gold projects hit another setback when a British Columbia court struck down the decision that kept an environmental approval from expiring.
B.C. must undertake deep consultation with the Tsetsaut Skii km Lax Ha Nation before it decides again whether construction at the KSM project had “substantially started,” B.C. Supreme Court Justice Emily Burke confirmed Nov. 18. Seabridge shares fell $10.72 , or 29%, to close at $25.92 in Toronto the next day, when the company disclosed the ruling. They were at $27.64 on Monday, valuing the company at $2.99 billion.
“We are very confident that KSM has more than met the requirements for a Substantially Started designation,” Seabridge CEO Rudi Fronk said in the company’s Nov. 19 statement on the ruling.
Seabridge faces the review amid competing First Nations claims, while a dispute with Tudor Gold (TSXV: TUD) holds up permits for the tunnels that would carry KSM ore to the mill. It still needs a partner to build the project and has a loan due at year-end.
Large potential
Seabridge’s 2022 prefeasibility study projected 1.03 million oz. of gold a year on average for 33 years. That’s 46% more than the roughly 706,000 oz. that Natural Resources Canada estimates all B.C. mines produced in 2025.
Burke clarified that her June ruling had quashed B.C.’s 2024 decision on the Golden Triangle copper-gold project, 65 km northwest of Stewart. Under provincial assessment rules , the certificate would stand for the life of the project if B.C. finds enough work took place by July 29 this year. The 2014 certificate remains in force during the review, Seabridge said.
Construction spending at KSM had topped $700 million (US$487 million) by July 29, up from $444 million when B.C. made its original decision, Seabridge said. The Nov. 18 drop erased about $1.16 billion in market value. Even after Monday’s 11% rebound, the shares were 25% below their $36.64 close the day before Seabridge disclosed the ruling.
First Nations
On Monday, the Nisga’a and Tahltan nations backed the original provincial decision and rejected the Tsetsaut Skii km Lax Ha Nation’s territorial claim at KSM. The project lies in Tahltan territory and in the Nass Area and Nass Wildlife Area covered by the Nisga’a treaty, the two nations said. Their development companies jointly own Treaty Creek Limited Partnership, which worked with BC Hydro on KSM’s power connection.
“We are the rights holders and decision makers for our respective Territories,” the Nisga’a and Tahltan said in a joint statement on KSM.
The Tsetsaut Skii km Lax Ha say the proposed tailings site stretches 9 km across their territory. In September, the nation called for a bonded fund to pay for cleanup and long-term water treatment. It also wants monitors it appoints to have the power to halt work at the site.
“Consultation means more than allowing us to speak,” Chief Darlene Simpson said at the time. “It means acting on our concerns as stewards of the land.”
Tunnel dispute
B.C. has deferred a decision on permits to build the full length of the twin Mitchell Treaty tunnels. They would carry ore from the Mitchell Valley to a processing plant in the Treaty Valley. About 12.5 km of the route crosses Tudor’s claims.
Tudor says the proposed route crosses both its Goldstorm deposit and Perfectstorm zone at Treaty Creek. It is challenging the province’s authority to reserve a tunnel corridor across claims Tudor says predate it. Seabridge says it has permits for limited work at the tunnel entrances and plans to finish a feasibility study before starting tunnel construction.
Seabridge estimated in 2022 that KSM would cost US$6.4 billion to build. It was planning next year’s field program with its preferred joint venture partner while the two negotiated a deal, the company said in its quarterly update this month. Fronk told The Northern Miner last year he expected to name a partner by the end of 2025.
Seabridge drew the remaining US$50 million on a US$100-million loan on Nov. 2. The full amount comes due Dec. 31 and can be repaid in cash or, with Toronto Stock Exchange approval, in shares, the company said in its quarterly filing this month.

All-Electric Porsche 718 Boxster Coming Out in Early 2027, Here's What It Brings
23 photos
Photo: Porsche
German carmaker Porsche is planning to start the new year with a hell of a bang. Sometime in the first three months of 2027, it will unveil the production version of its first all-electric two-door sports car, the new 718 Boxster.
Although in most ways that matter the new vehicle is based on the 911, its electric powertrain required some innovative thinking, especially in the way it is designed and integrated into the car. Why so? Well, for the simple reason that Porsche wanted the 718 to retain its mid-engine driving dynamics and low seating position, despite the fact that there is now no actual engine to speak of.
The carmaker calls the solution the E-Core, and it's been in the news, on and off, for about five years already. For the purposes of its use in the 718, it translates to the placement of the battery pack directly behind the car's two seats, the location where Porsche usually mounts some of the internal combustion engines it still uses.
Putting the 800-volt battery there allows the driver's seat height to be kept as low as required from a sports car, while at the same time making sure the bulk of the vehicle's weight is kept towards the middle.
There is talk of a 40 percent front and 60 percent rear weight distribution - a total weight that's not fully disclosed yet, but is similar to the present-day 911 Cabriolets that employ the T-Hybrid powertrain. In numbers, that could be anywhere between 3,693 pounds (1,675 kg) and 3,990 pounds (1,810 kg).
Photo: Porsche I said earlier that the new 718 Boxster is heavily based on the 911, and that is more obvious than anywhere when talking about the chassis components: steering, including, for the first time on this model, rear-axle steering, braking system, and even the electronically controlled limited-slip differential.
What is not derived from tech used on the 911 is, aside from the purpose-made E-Core solution, the vehicle's electric powertrain. Porsche does not go into the specifics of what that means, yet, but it does talk about an acceleration time from zero to 62 mph of under three seconds for the top-of-the-range model, and top speeds of 155 mph (250 kph).
We don't know at the moment how many versions of the electric car will be available, but Porsche confirmed that all of them will be rear-wheel drive and, on top of everything, will be equipped with something called the E-Shift.
It's a term you may be familiar with since the summer of this year, when the 2027 Taycan broke cover. Essentially, we're dealing with a virtual gearbox, more specifically the seven-speed PDK transmission that would normally be used in an ICE vehicle.
Photo: Porsche What the tech does is allow the driver to choose between automatic gear changes or manual shifts, achieved by using the paddles placed behind the steering wheel. For the purpose of tricking the senses, when the car is in E-Shift mode (people can choose not to enable it), the 718 also replicates the sounds of a six-cylinder boxer engine makes when shifting gears.
It's a lie, true, but a beautiful one, as the car whose sounds it replicates is none other than the 981-generation Boxster GTS .
I said earlier that people can choose not to enable this make-believe feature, and when that happens, the steering wheel paddles can be used to select one of three stages of energy recuperation.
We know all of these new details because Porsche shared them this week under the guise of an announcement detailing the extensive testing program the electric 718 Boxster has been subjected to. And this program is equally as impressive as the car itself.
Photo: Porsche The Germans claim to have traveled close to 2.5 million miles (four million km) with test vehicles, subjecting them to temperatures as low as minus 22 degrees Fahrenheit (minus 30 degrees Celsius) in Sweden and as high as 124 degrees Fahrenheit (51 degrees Celsius) in Death Valley.
Test 781s (unclear how many of them) covered the miles above both in the wild and in very crowded cities like Las Vegas , Los Angeles, and Shanghai, from as low as 279 feet (86 meters) below sea level to 9,022 feet (2,750 meters) above it, traveling in the process to some 20 countries.
Most of this journey has been documented on film and uploaded online so that we all can get a glimpse of what it meant. You can find the first episode of the documentary, called " The new 718 Boxster: a development story," attached below this text.
Porsche describes the new, electric 718 Boxster as an entry-level vehicle to its range of two-door sports cars. It will assemble it at the main facility in Stuttgart-Zuffenhausen, with the lines expected to start rolling soon. We will keep an eye on things and report back once we know more about the newcomer.

GLASGOW, Scotland — Russia may place a satellite loaded with a nuclear weapon into orbit by the end of the year, German public media reported, citing intelligence sources.
The satellite, dubbed Sputnik-S, has reportedly been assembled and stored in the greater Moscow area for several years. An investigation by German public broadcasters WDR and NDR and German newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung uncovered an intelligence assessment from early November that says the satellite could be launched “within 60 days.”
Asked about the reporting during a visit to Berlin, NATO chief Mark Rutte said on Monday that the alliance was constantly assessing its deterrence and defence situation.
“I can assure you, we will always make sure that we defend every inch of NATO territory. And that includes making sure that we are safe when it comes to the space element,” Rutte told reporters at a joint press conference with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
Placing a nuclear weapon in orbit is prohibited by the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, to which Russia and 117 other countries are parties.
Detonating an atomic bomb in space can have devastating effects: It is likely to destroy or incapacitate a large number of satellites, as well as cripple communications systems and power grids back on Earth with its electromagnetic pulse.
Both the United States and the Soviet Union detonated nuclear weapons in space during the Cold War, most significantly the American Starfish Prime test, 400 kilometers over the Pacific Ocean in 1962. The resulting artificial radiation belt damaged several satellites, including the Telstar-1 satellite launched a day after the blast.
Reporting by Western intelligence agencies of alleged Russian plans to place a nuke into orbit dates back several years. In early 2024, then-House Intelligence Committee chairman Mike Turner (R-Ohio) publicly warned of a “serious national security threat” without identifying it; U.S. media soon reported this was referring to a Russian space nuke. The U.S. intelligence community reportedly started circulating corresponding warnings a year earlier, in February 2023, German public media reports.
Shortly before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, a mysterious satellite called simply Kosmos-2553 was launched, which Western governments had flagged as a potential space threat. Kosmos is the generic identifier for unnamed Russian satellites, including military ones with undisclosed functions.
The Russian authorities said Kosmos-2553 was for scientific research into radiation. However, Western intelligence agencies were “greatly skeptical” of this civilian explanation, according to the new reporting by German media.
Security services told WDR and NDR that they believe the satellite was being used to test the effects of nuclear weapons use in space. According to them, the satellite “functions as a so-called dummy, intended to test how radiation affects satellites – and at what point a satellite sustains severe damage.” The aim of the tests was to determine the extent to which the satellite remains operational and maneuverable under intense radiation.
The Russian Embassy in Berlin said it had no information on the topic, and said it rejected all accusations regarding the space activities of the Russian Federation, calling them part of a “propaganda campaign,” reporters from WDR, NDR and Süddeutsche Zeitung wrote. Russian measures for the exploration and utilization of space are conducted in accordance with international commitments and “exclusively for peaceful purposes,” the Embassy said.

Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX are working toward a year-end deadline to agree on their all-stock merger, according to the Financial Times. A signed deal by December 31 would land days before the new Congress, where Democrats have promised to dig into Musk’s companies, is sworn in on January 3.
The FT also named the directors negotiating for each side. Two of Tesla’s three are the same people who designed Musk’s $1 trillion pay package.
We’ve been tracking the Tesla-SpaceX merger since Musk first floated it in May, when we called it Musk’s fourth billion-dollar self-deal , and his first trillion-dollar self-deal. Earlier this month, Bloomberg reported that SpaceX could announce the deal as soon as December . The FT report adds a deadline, names and a vote threshold.
A year-end deadline, and January 3
According to the FT, the talks are “moving towards a potential year-end deadline,” even though people familiar with the negotiations say an agreement isn’t close. The combined group would be worth about $3.5 trillion, by far the largest merger ever.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
So why year-end? Look at the calendar.
The new Congress is seated on January 3. As of November 24, AP’s count has Democrats at 258 House seats and 56 Senate seats. Democrats haven’t been subtle about what comes next: Sen. Ruben Gallego tagged Musk on X with “See you in January,” and SpaceX’s military contracts and Musk’s Starlink decisions over Ukraine are expected to be early investigation targets.
It’s not only Washington. Texas’ incoming attorney general told Bloomberg that a merger of this size “warrants tremendous scrutiny,” and Bloomberg had previously reported that the companies want to close before President Trump leaves office.
Who’s at the table
Tesla’s special committee is chair Robyn Denholm, Kathleen Wilson-Thompson and Jack Hartung, advised by Evercore. SpaceX is represented by Roelof Botha and Randy Glein, with Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs as advisers. Both banks also helped take SpaceX public in June.
Denholm and Wilson-Thompson should sound familiar. They were the two-person special committee that built Musk’s new CEO pay package after a Delaware judge voided his 2018 award. And that 2025 award has change-in-control terms that drop its operational milestones and vest earned shares at the deal price, so the committee that wrote it is now negotiating the deal that could trigger it.
Ira Ehrenpreis, a long-time friend of Musk, who chairs Tesla’s compensation and governance committees and has sat on SpaceX’s board since February, isn’t on Tesla’s committee, per the FT.
If you can believe it, Musk isn’t formally in the room. The FT says Texas governance rules keep him out of active negotiations, but both committees can consult senior executives for information. Every one of those executives reports to Musk.
The vote math
Any agreement goes to a separate extraordinary Tesla shareholder meeting, and it needs more than 50% of all outstanding votes, not just of votes cast. Abstentions and uncast shares effectively count as “no.”
That sounds like a high bar. But Musk holds about 20% of Tesla’s voting power, and nothing in the report says his shares will be excluded. If they count, he’s 40% of the way to approval before a single other shareholder votes. On the other side, Musk controls about 84% of SpaceX’s votes, so there’s no real suspense there.
Uncast retail votes are exactly what Tesla’s new auto-vote program, rolled out in its October proxy, was designed to reduce.
Then there’s the regulatory side. The FT says the deal could draw scrutiny in the US, China, Europe and the UK, with Tesla’s China operations sitting awkwardly next to SpaceX’s rocket and Starlink business, which does a lot of work for the US military. Giga Shanghai builds more than half of Tesla’s cars.
Electrek’s Take
Congress can’t block this merger. Antitrust review sits with Trump’s DOJ and FTC until 2029, plus China, the EU and the UK.
What congressional committees can do is subpoena. Committee minutes, the Evercore fairness work, emails between Denholm’s committee and Musk’s executives about how the exchange ratio got set. That’s the kind of record that got Musk’s 2018 pay package voided by a Delaware judge, and it’s the kind of record nobody wants dragged into a hearing mid-negotiation.
The talks are “not close,” yet there’s a deadline. When the deadline comes from the political calendar instead of the negotiation, the side that wants to close fast is the one giving ground. But in this case, Musk is both sides, but he is mainly SpaceX.
We’ve said it before, and we’ll keep saying it: the only vote that means anything here is a majority of Tesla shareholders not named Musk. Denholm, who is up for re-election at next week’s December 3 annual meeting, could commit to that today, but in her entire tenure as Tesla chair, she always did exactly what Musk wanted.

By: Northern Miner Staff November 24, 2026
I-80 Gold (TSX: IAU; NYSE: IAUX) has begun mining at Archimedes, its second underground gold mine in Nevada, saying it expects to recover the first Archimedes gold from its Ruby Hill leach pad in next year’s first quarter.
Most of the material mined next year should be oxide that i-80 can leach on site near Eureka, the company said Monday . Its earlier plan called for mostly sulphide material processed by a third party, with payment for 58% of the contained gold. I-80 now plans to stockpile refractory sulphide material for its own Lone Tree plant, which is scheduled for commissioning in the fourth quarter of 2027.
“A lower-cost oxide route supports near-term cash flow ahead of Lone Tree, though the contribution remains subject to quantification with 2027 guidance,” National Bank Financial mining analyst Don DeMarco wrote in a note Tuesday.
Some of the oxide lies outside the mineral resource estimate supporting the preliminary economic assessment and hasn’t been classified as resources or reserves. I-80 expects to issue production guidance early next year. Expanded surface infrastructure is expected to lift total project capital to approximately $57.3 million (C$82 million), about 21% more than the $47.3-million estimate that was contained in a March 2025 assessment.
Ruby Hill property
Archimedes is part of the wholly owned Ruby Hill property, which i-80 acquired in 2021. Construction of the underground project began in September 2025. The company has completed about 3,600 metres of lateral development, and work on additional ventilation, change facilities and offices will continue through 2027 as mining rates increase.
The underground mine targets the 426 and Ruby Deeps zones. The 2025 assessment outlined roughly a decade of mining and average annual gold output of about 100,000 oz. after ramp-up. The company reported indicated resources of 1.8 million tonnes grading 7.6 grams gold per tonne and inferred resources of 4.2 million tonnes grading 7.3 grams gold per tonne as of the end of 2025.
Heap leaching provides a route to recover gold from oxide material before Lone Tree is ready. Refractory sulphide material needs more intensive treatment. I-80 expects a significant oxide contribution at Archimedes over the next three years, although the size of that contribution has not yet been quantified in production guidance.
Seven underground rigs are drilling the lower 426 and Ruby Deeps zones in a programme of about 55,000 metres across 140 holes. Completion is expected in the second quarter of 2027, supporting a feasibility study in the second half. After Lone Tree is commissioned, i-80 targets combined annual production of 150,000–200,000 oz. from Archimedes and Granite Creek beginning in 2028.
I-80 shares dropped 1.3% to C$1.52 Tuesday morning in Toronto, valuing the company at about C$1.3 billion ($922 million). The stock has traded between C$1.34 and C$3.04 in the past year.

EU Imposes 200-Day Import Quotas on Hybrid Vehicles Produced in China, Japan, UK, US, and More
29 photos
Photo: MG
As expected, the European Union has decided on limiting imports of new hybrid passenger cars from a bunch of major exporting countries. The quota system will go into effect on December 1, 2026, and run through June 18, 2027, introducing a 200-day safeguard that covers full hybrids, plug-in hybrids, and mild hybrids.
Regulation 2026/2614 clearly states that additional qualifying vehicles from a given country are prohibited from entering the European bloc once an individual quota runs out. The union's trade measure affects China, Japan, the United Kingdom, the United States, Turkey, South Korea, Mexico, Morocco, South Africa, Serbia, and other countries.
Only 822 vehicles are listed under the 'other countries' quota, but more curiously, South Africa is listed as 'not applicable'. On closer inspection, South Africa is omitted from Annex I.2, which lists developing countries that exceed the 3 percent EU hybrid import threshold.
In other words, South African-built hybrids are exempt for the time being from the provisional safeguard that European legislators designed to protect European automakers. Brussels introduced this safeguard as a response to rising imports from outside the bloc, imports that are often more affordable than European hybrids.
The European Commission points to falling domestic market share and deteriorating profitability as well, which is crazy when you remember that hybrid vehicles are increasingly popular across the European space. If you ask me, high prices and pitiful quality both hinder European automakers right now.
There's also the matter of high energy costs and high labor costs, of course, but on the ground, it's hard to make a case for the shoddy interior plastics and the poor after-sales service of many European automakers. China gets the largest piece of the pie, with Japan not far behind. For all countries, the Commission has divided the restriction into three separate periods.
Photo: MG These run from December 1, 2026, through February 28, 2027, then March 1 through May 31, and June 1 through June 18. All told, China received a total allowance of 191,780 hybrids across those 200 days. Japan got 170,899 vehicles, while Turkey received 126,320 across all three periods. The United Kingdom and South Korea got 105,402 and 67,924 vehicles.
Mexico couldn't do better than 34,755 vehicles, Morocco 23,954, Serbia 19,353, and the United States 18,482. Combined, total allocations amount to 759,681 vehicles for the entire 200-day period. Each country-specific quota is based on 2025 import volumes, adding slightly more than 15 percent.
Countries that accounted for more than 2 percent of European hybrid imports during 2025 received individual allocations. Unused quantities are to carry over in the following period, thus preventing manufacturers from losing access to an allocation because they didn't make the best of the initial three-month period.
Per regulation 2026/2614, customs authorities determine the hybrid vehicle's origin under the EU's non-preferential origin rules. This, in turn, makes the actual production location and applicable origin criteria extremely important. Chinese exporters, which pose the biggest threat to Europe's automotive industry, face an additional requirement.
Importers seeking access to China's allocation must present a signed and stamped export quota certificate issued by the CCCME, namely the China Chamber of Commerce for Import and Export of Machinery and Electronic Products. Otherwise put, the CCCME is in total control of dividing up the hard cap of 191,780 Chinese-built hybrids .

Rare 1971 Plymouth Hemi Road Runner Flaunts Even Rarer Color Combo
8 photos
Photo: Geoff Stunkard's Zookeeper's Diary/YouTube
Unlike the Dodge Super Bee , which was discontinued after the 1971 model year, the Plymouth Road Runner remained in production for a few more years. However, 1971 was the end of the line for high-compression Road Runners, as Chrysler discontinued those engines altogether.
Mopar's decision put an end to the 440-cubic-inch (7.2-liter) Six-Barrel V8. The 390-horsepower powerplant had only been introduced in mid-1969. More importantly, the mighty 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi also went into the history books in 1971, after six model years on the options list.
1971 was the lowest production year for the 425-horsepower engine. Existing records suggest that only 355 vehicles were ordered with this mill in the US; the figure includes six nameplates. The Cuda is the most common, with 114 examples made, while the Super Bee is the rarest, with just 22 produced. The Road Runner you see here is one of only 55 units built.
The Mopar was recently showcased at the 2026 Muscle Car and Corvette Nationals (MCACN) , where it made its first public appearance after an extensive restoration. There's no info on whether it's a manual or automatic car, which keeps the actual production number under wraps. Of the 55 units made, 27 were fitted with the three-speed TorqueFlite automatic, while the remaining 28 examples got the four-speed manual.
But this car is rare regardless of the transmission, and I'd dare say ultra-rare when we factor in the color combo. The Road Runner is finished in Bahama Yellow, a somewhat brownish shade of yellow that was part of the Mopar high-impact color palette. Called Butterscotch on Dodge models, Bahama Yellow was only offered between 1969 and 1971.
The hue is rarer than the flashier high-impact colors, but it's the interior that sets this vehicle apart. The original owner went with a two-tone combo combining black and orange. The option was brand-new for 1971 and was discontinued for 1972. The combo is widely known as Halloween, though Plymouth did not use this name.
Historians label this interior as relatively uncommon. I've seen it in a few Mopars in recent years, but never combined with a Bahama Yellow exterior . The owner describes this Road Runner as a one-of-one. It may also have to do with a few other options (too bad we can't see the window sticker), but the color combo is probably the main culprit here.
The vehicle was restored by Apex Auto Restoration, and, needless to say, it looks flawless at first glance. It's probably one of the finest 1971 Hemi rigs out there, and I do hope we'll get a more detailed walkaround soon. Until that happens, you can see it making its first public appearance in restored condition by hitting the play button below.
By the way, these 1971 Road Runners can get pretty expensive when fitted with a 426 Hemi engine . They usually fetch over $150,000, but some examples can trade for significantly more than that. As of this writing, the most expensive units sold for $242,000 (2025) and a whopping $550,000 (2023).
